children: Jefferies defended Life Time Group Holdings
after the introduction of Meta Musa this week created an initial wave of selling.
Analyst Randal Konik noted the Muse headlines had investors considering a churn impact to Life Time's
premium membership flywheel. Konik noted that cancellation has always been easy for Life Time
customers, so there is no friction for Muse to remove.

"Muse attacks friction, and although it's a powerful tool, it is unable to complete a cancellation of an LTH membership. The tools that help consumers shed subscriptions will work best against forgotten, low-dollar, low-engagement autopays that survive on save offers, automated retention tactics, and phone-tree gauntlets," wrote Konik. "Members on average pay ~$245 in dues per month, ~3x the industry average, walk into a resort-style club >150 times a year, and re-underwrite that decision every time they swipe in," he added. Konik and his team concluded that the market is conflating a subscription-economy problem with a usage-economy business.
Jefferies kept its Buy rating on Life Time Group
Shares of LTH slipped 0.5% in premarket trading on Friday. The 52-week high for the stock is $47.24. The Seeking Alpha Quant Rating on LTH is flashing Strong Buy.

title: Jefferies says Meta's AI agent is not a threat to Life Time
